documents.name: pharmacist_notes.txt
documents.text:
The system must require two-factor authentication for all pharmacist logins. 
Schedule H1 sales must be logged with patient name and prescriber details.

requirements.statement: The system must require two-factor authentication for all pharmacist logins.
requirements.source_quote: The system must require two-factor authentication for all pharmacist logins.
requirements.justification: Protects regulated records and patient data from misuse.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user without the required role, the action is denied and the attempt is logged.

regulations.title: Information security controls - access control, logging, secure operation
regulations.source: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A (access control, logging, cryptography) and OWASP ASVS

requirements.statement: Schedule H1 sales must be logged with patient name and prescriber details.
requirements.source_quote: Schedule H1 sales must be logged with patient name and prescriber details.
requirements.justification: Supports regulatory compliance and inspection readiness.
acceptance_criteria: Given a scheduled drug is dispensed, when the sale is confirmed, then a register entry with patient, prescriber, drug, batch, quantity and date exists.
A user cannot complete the sale while a mandatory register field is empty.
Given a prescription with a missing mandatory field, the system refuses to continue and lists the missing fields.

regulations.title: Drugs and Cosmetics Rules - Schedule H1 drugs (separate register)
regulations.source: Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 (Schedule H1, inserted 2013-14)
regulations.rationale: Matched terms: h1, name, patient, prescriber, schedule

regulations.title: Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 - Schedule H drugs (sale on prescription)
regulations.source: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules, 1945 (Rule 65 and Schedule H)
regulations.rationale: Matched terms: name, patient, prescriber, sale, schedule

gaps.description: Block sale of Schedule H drugs without a valid prescription
gaps.suggested_requirement: The system shall not allow a Schedule H drug to be dispensed unless a valid prescription is attached to the sale.

gaps.description: Maintain a separate Schedule H1 register entry for each supply
gaps.suggested_requirement: The system shall create a Schedule H1 register entry (patient, prescriber, drug, batch, quantity, date) for every H1 dispensing.

gaps.description: Retain H1 records for the legally required period
gaps.suggested_requirement: The system shall retain Schedule H1 register entries for the legally required period (to be confirmed by the compliance officer) and prevent their deletion.

gaps.description: Retain a copy of the prescription for Schedule X supply
gaps.suggested_requirement: The system shall store a copy of the prescription for every Schedule X supply and link it to the register entry.
The system shall record every Schedule X supply in the scheduled-drug register.

gaps.description: Accurate stock and supply records for NDPS substances
gaps.suggested_requirement: The system shall keep an accurate stock and supply record for NDPS substances and support inspection reports.

gaps.description: Produce purchase/sale records for the inspector
gaps.suggested_requirement: The system shall produce purchase, sale and scheduled-drug records on demand for a drug inspector.

gaps.description: Pharmacist verification step before handing over the drug
gaps.suggested_requirement: The system shall require an explicit pharmacist verification step (drug, strength, quantity, batch) before a dispensing is completed.
The system shall record every drug substitution with the original drug, the substitute, the reason and the approving pharmacist.

gaps.description: Collect only needed patient data, for a stated purpose
gaps.suggested_requirement: The system shall collect only the patient data needed for dispensing and record the purpose and consent status.

gaps.description: Protect personal data (access control, encryption, masking)
gaps.suggested_requirement: The system shall protect patient and prescription data with role-based access, encryption in transit and at rest, and masking in non-clinical views.
The system shall log access to patient data and support breach investigation and notification.

gaps.description: Audit trail with user, time and reason for every record change
gaps.suggested_requirement: The system shall keep an audit trail (user, timestamp, old value, new value, reason) for every change to dispensing, stock and register records.

gaps.description: Prevent deletion or silent overwrite of regulated records
gaps.suggested_requirement: The system shall prevent deletion of regulated records; corrections shall be added as new entries that reference the original.
The system shall enforce role-based access control with least privilege for pharmacist, assistant, owner and auditor roles.

risks.title: Incomplete or missing scheduled-drug register entry (inspection finding)
risks.mitigation: Register entry is created atomically with the sale; mandatory fields enforced.

risks.title: Unauthorised access to patient or prescription data
risks.mitigation: RBAC, least privilege, MFA for privileged actions, encryption, access logging.

risks.title: LLM hallucination invents a requirement or a rule
risks.mitigation: Grounding check on every proposal (verbatim quote), RAG citations, confidence scores, human approval.

risks.title: Outdated or wrong regulatory text in the knowledge base
risks.mitigation: Versioned KB, 'verified' flag, official source check before use, regulator-facing claims need human sign-off.
risks.verification: KB review checklist before each release.

risks.title: Over-trust: AI output treated as legal or clinical advice
risks.mitigation: Scope guard, 'candidate mapping' wording, mandatory approvals by qualified roles.

risks.title: Schedule lists or rules change and software is out of date
risks.mitigation: Configurable schedule lists with versioning and an owner for change control.
risks.verification: Change-control drill: update list, verify behaviour.

risks.title: Prompt injection through uploaded stakeholder documents
risks.mitigation: Input screening, untrusted-text delimiters, JSON-only outputs, no tool access for agents.
risks.verification: Injection test document in the sample set.

risks.title: Sensitive data sent to an LLM
risks.mitigation: PII masking before any LLM call; synthetic data only in the prototype.

risks.title: Personal data used beyond purpose / not minimised
risks.mitigation: Collect minimum data; purpose and consent recorded; masking in non-clinical views.

rules_fired: R1: patient-safety impact and regulatory criticality are both high -> pure Agile capped at 60 (it does not give validation evidence on its own).
R4: stable requirements and high verification need -> bonus for V-Model/Waterfall.
R7: validated-system expectations -> Waterfall penalised for late verification and slow response to rule changes.
sdlc.explanation: V-Model ranks first (91.0%). Best-matching drivers: need for formal verification and evidence 0.85 (target 0.95); regulatory criticality 1.00 (target 0.90); patient-safety impact of failure 1.00 (target 0.90); requirement stability 0.84 (target 0.75). Runner-up: Waterfall (81.6%). Rules applied: R1 R4 R7. Final adoption needs approval from the project manager, architect, security lead and compliance officer.

workflow.name: Planning and validation plan
activities: Confirm scope: prescription-to-dispensing with scheduled-drug register
Agree roles, tools, risk-based validation plan
Set up requirement baseline and change-control process
compliance_checkpoints: Compliance officer confirms applicable rules list

workflow.name: Requirements and hazard analysis
activities: Hazard analysis: wrong drug, expired batch, missing register entry
compliance_checkpoints: Every regulatory requirement has a cited source

workflow.name: Architecture and design with threat modelling
activities: Threat model: unauthorised override, record tampering, data leakage
Define audit-trail and register data model
exit_criteria: Every requirement allocated to a design element

workflow.name: Implementation
compliance_checkpoints: Safety-critical code reviewed by a second developer
workflow.gate: Increment done: tests and scans pass

workflow.name: Verification (unit, integration, system)
activities: Regression suite for dispensing and register
V-mapping: unit tests <-> module design, integration tests <-> architecture, system tests <-> SRS, UAT <-> user needs
security_controls: Security tests of override and access paths
compliance_checkpoints: Each requirement linked to a passed test

workflow.name: Validation with pharmacists
activities: Dispensing-accuracy test set (including expired, recalled, H1/X cases)
User acceptance testing by a pharmacist
Mock inspection using the generated reports

workflow.name: Compliance approval and release
exit_criteria: Approvals recorded in the audit trail

workflow.name: Operation and change control
activities: Update schedule lists and rules under change control
